concerns.text: FR-003 and Plan 'Synthetic Data Fallback' require the system to generate a synthetic dataset if verified US sources are absent. Tasks T027/T028 describe generating null models from 'theoretical priors' but no task exists to implement the 'Synthetic Data Fallback' ingestion/generation logic (e.g., a script to create synthetic precinct/county vote data with known ground truth) required to validate the methodology when real data is missing.

FR-005 and Plan 'Sensitivity Analysis Thresholds' explicitly define the sensitivity sweep set as '{[deferred], [deferred], [deferred], [deferred]}' (or a set where specific values are deferred). Task T039 hardcodes a specific set '{0.01%, 0.05%, 0.1%, 0.5%}'. This task does not cover the requirement to implement the logic for deferred/variable thresholds as mandated by the spec, effectively pre-asserting empirical values that the spec requires to be deferred.

SC-006 (Success Criterion) states VIF calculation applies 'if multiple predictors... are used in any extended analysis'. Task T035 unconditionally implements VIF calculation. There is no task to implement the conditional check ('if predictors exist') or to handle the 'Not Applicable' case defined in the Plan, creating a gap in covering the conditional nature of SC-006.

Plan 'Reproducibility' and Constitution Principle I require verification on a 'fresh GitHub Actions runner'. Task T009 implements a `--verify-reproducible` flag to 're-run analysis on a clean environment' (implied local). There is no task to implement the CI-specific logic (e.g., GitHub Actions workflow trigger or runner isolation check) required to satisfy the 'fresh runner' constraint of the Plan and Constitution.

FR-005 requires a single sensitivity analysis that sweeps thresholds AND compares null models, 'reporting the variation in flagged jurisdiction counts' across both dimensions. Tasks T039 (thresholds) and T040 (models) are split. While they cover the components, there is no explicit task to implement the 'unified report' logic that correlates variation across both dimensions simultaneously as required by the spec's 'reporting' clause.
